snippet.title: The Secret History of the Handshake
snippet.description:
At some point today, you will probably shake someone's hand. The gesture is so automatic you perform it without thinking — two people extend their right hands, grip, shake twice, release.

It takes about three seconds. In those three seconds, you are performing a ritual that is at least twenty-five hundred years old — one that began not as a greeting but as proof you weren't holding a weapon, was adopted by merchants to seal deals with no written contract, and was spread across the world partly by a pacifist religious sect from seventeenth-century England.

This is the hidden history of a gesture so universal it now feels like instinct — and isn't.
